newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Croat general to stand trial for war crimes.
newsitem.headline: Croat general to stand trial for war crimes.

text.p: A Bosnian Croat militia leader will stand trial for war crimes early next year, the U.N. tribunal for former Yugoslavia said on Friday.
The trial of General Tihomir Blaskic, charged with crimes against Moslem civilians in 1992 and 1993, is due to start on January 8, a tribunal spokewsoman said.
Blaskic gave himself up to the tribunal on April 1 under pressure from the Croatian government which itself had come under U.S. pressure to hand him over for trial.
He subsequently pleaded not guilty to charges of crimes allegedly committed against Moslems when he was commander of Bosnian Croat forces in the Lasva Valley region of Bosnia.
The 1995 indictment issued against Blaskic said the Croats' "ethnic cleansing" was so thorough that almost all of the area's Moslem population was killed or driven away.
Bosnian Croats and Moslems were nominal allies in the war against separatist Bosnian Serb forces which began in 1992.
But a year later Croat forces turned against the Moslems and began to fight for "pure" Croat territory.
The village of Ahmici, near Vitez, was virtually destroyed by Croats in April 1993. Scores of Moslem civilians were killed, including children who appeared to have been burned alive.
Blaskic was promoted to a senior post in Croatia's regular army after his indictment by the Hague-based tribunal.
In all the tribunal has indicted 15 Croats for alleged atrocities committed in the central Bosnian Lasva Valley.
So far the tribunal has indicted over 70 Serbs, Croats and Moslems for alleged war crimes -- but has only seven in custody.
The first trial, of Bosnian Serb Dusan Tadic, began in May and is expected to continue until November, with a verdict expected early next year.
